# DRAFT: Arbeline research: nearly two-thirds of mid-market finance teams are still buried in manual invoice entry

DENVER, Nov. 6, 2026 -- A new survey of 400 U.S. finance decision-makers from Arbeline, the AP automation
company, finds that 64% say their AP team spends too much time on manual invoice entry, and that teams using AP
automation close their books 2.3 days faster than those without.

"We spent three days every month keying invoices by hand at our Loveland plant," said an assistant controller at
a Colorado manufacturer who took part in the survey. "Our auditors started asking why the close slipped."

Methodology: online survey of 400 U.S. finance decision-makers at companies with $50 million to $1 billion in
revenue, fielded October 19-30, 2026 by Penmore Research. The margin of error is +/-4.9 percentage points.

versions.content:
# Q3 2026 win/loss by primary competitor (Salesforce, 80 closed opportunities)

| Primary competitor | Closed | Won | Win rate | Top loss reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kitecount | 23 | 14 | 60.9% | price (6 of 9 losses) |
| Tallyroute | 19 | 8 | 42.1% | features (5 of 11) |
| Noventa | 7 | 3 | 3 of 7 | too few to say |
| None recorded | 31 | 22 | 71.0% | no decision (5 of 9) |
| All | 80 | 47 | 58.8% | price 12 of 33 losses (36.4%) |

Read: (1) Tallyroute is our hardest named competitor, and we lose to them on features (5 of 11 losses) more than on price; with their $60M round going into multi-entity approvals, expect that gap to close. (2) Against Kitecount we win most deals, and the losses are price; their move to per-invoice pricing on 11/2 makes them dearer for high-volume prospects, so ask about invoice volume early. (3) 31 of 80 deals (38.8%) have no competitor recorded, so every number here is directional; making the field required at stage 3 would fix it.
Caveats: one quarter, rep-entered fields, no significance testing at these sizes.
versions.note: wrote the Q3 win/loss read for Wendy

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# Awareness and consideration (Q3a/Q3b, valid n=400)

| Vendor | Aware | Would consider | Consider, of those aware |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kitecount | 49.0% (196) | 18.5% (74) | 37.8% |
| Arbeline | 41.0% (164) | 21.5% (86) | 52.4% |
| Tallyroute | 37.8% (151) | 15.3% (61) | 40.4% |
| Noventa | 22.0% (88) | 7.5% (30) | 34.1% |

Headline: fewer finance leaders know Arbeline than Kitecount, but those who do are the most likely to consider us (52% vs 38%), so more of them consider Arbeline overall. Awareness is the constraint, not appeal.
Note: the same respondents rate every vendor, so the gaps aren't independent samples; treat them as directional unless Penmore runs paired tests on the row-level Q3 data. Opt-in panel; no margin of error.
